company.name: Maple & Sage Dental
company.summary: Maple & Sage Dental runs three dental clinics in Leeds, UK. Your team of about 40 provides check-ups, hygiene, general treatments, appointment booking, insurance support, and treatment plans for local patients.
offerings: Routine dental check-ups and hygiene appointments
General dental treatments such as fillings and root canals
company.customers: Local patients in Leeds, including families, adults, and children. Some treatment is paid privately or through insurance.
tech_signals: Practice management software (not named in brief)

roles.title: Dentist

roles.title: Dental nurse
repetitive_tasks: Turning over treatment rooms between patients

roles.title: Receptionist
repetitive_tasks: Answering phone calls and booking appointments
Taking payments and handling insurance questions

roles.title: Practice manager
repetitive_tasks: Building staff rotas across three clinics

roles.title: Admin assistant
repetitive_tasks: Filing insurance forms and patient documents
Entering patient data into the practice system

strategy.situation: Maple & Sage Dental runs three dental clinics in Leeds with about 40 staff, offering check-ups, hygiene, general treatments, emergency appointments, insurance support, and treatment plans.
strategy.complication: Appointment calls, reminders, insurance claims, and clinical admin still depend on manual work across three sites, which slows patient response, risks missed follow-ups, and takes your team away from chairside care.
strategy.governing_thought: Start with the front desk appointment agent, the recall reminder agent, and the insurance claim agent, so your team cuts the most repetitive admin and proves value before expanding.

key_arguments.headline: Front desk, recall admin, and insurance claims absorb most of the repetitive work.
key_arguments.support: Receptionists handle calls, reschedules, reminders, payments, and insurance questions while also managing the desk. Admin assistants send recall letters and file documents, and finance assistants submit claims and chase balances. These tasks are frequent, rule-based, and spread across all three clinics, so delays show up in bookings, no-shows, and unpaid claims.

key_arguments.headline: These three agents are quick to set up and target visible daily pain.
key_arguments.support: Appointment booking and recall reminders use existing phone, email, and reminder tools, so they need little integration. Insurance claim preparation follows a predictable form and falls between finance and front desk, where errors cost time. Together they cover patient contact, follow-up, and payment, the three areas your team feels first.

key_arguments.headline: Roll out in stages, keep humans in control, and measure before expanding.
key_arguments.support: Start with one clinic or one workflow, train the small group who will use it, and review outputs daily for the first two weeks. Human staff approve bookings, claim submissions, and reminder wording until accuracy is proven. After that, extend the same agents to the other clinics and add clinical and rota support.

strategy.executive_summary: Maple & Sage Dental runs three dental clinics in Leeds with about 40 staff, offering check-ups, hygiene, general treatments, emergency appointments, insurance support, and treatment plans. Appointment calls, reminders, insurance claims, and clinical admin still depend on manual work across three sites, which slows patient response, risks missed follow-ups, and takes your team away from chairside care. Start with the front desk appointment agent, the recall reminder agent, and the insurance claim agent, so your team cuts the most repetitive admin and proves value before expanding.

maturity.label: Early
maturity.note: Tools are mostly manual with practice software and reminders in place. A few simple automations could be added without a big IT project.

opportunities.title: Appointment requests answered and booked from calls and web forms
opportunities.description: An agent answers routine booking, rescheduling, and cancellation requests from phone messages, email, and web forms, then proposes open slots. It checks the practice system for availability and sends confirmation, while staff handle complex or clinical questions.
before: Patient calls or emails the clinic
Receptionist listens to voicemail or reads email
Staff checks the booking system for open slots
Receptionist calls or emails the patient back
Staff manually enters or changes the appointment
after: Patient calls, emails, or uses a web form
Agent captures the request and checks the booking system
Agent proposes two or three open slots and confirms the choice
Human: Receptionist reviews and handles complex or clinical questions
Agent logs the booking and sends a confirmation

opportunities.title: Recall letters and appointment reminders sent on schedule
opportunities.description: An agent builds the daily recall and reminder list from the practice system, drafts the message, and sends it by the patient's preferred channel. It tracks replies and books simple recall appointments or flags them for staff.
before: Staff checks which patients are due for recall
Admin assistant filters the patient list in the practice system
Staff writes or updates reminder letters and emails
Admin assistant sends reminders one by one
Staff logs replies and books follow-ups manually
after: Agent pulls the daily recall and reminder list from the practice system
Agent drafts and sends reminders by email or text
Patient replies with a preferred time
Agent offers slots and books simple recall appointments
Human: Admin assistant handles special cases and confirms with hygienist

opportunities.title: Insurance claims prepared and submitted with fewer errors
opportunities.description: An agent gathers treatment codes, patient details, and insurer rules, then prepares the claim form for review. It submits approved claims and logs the status so staff can chase only the exceptions.
before: Finance assistant collects treatment details from the practice system
Staff checks the insurer's claim rules and patient policy
Finance assistant fills in the claim form
Finance manager reviews and approves the claim
Staff submits the claim and records the reference
after: Agent collects treatment and patient details from the practice system
Agent checks the insurer rules and flags missing information
Agent prepares the claim form and reference
Human: Finance assistant reviews and approves the claim
Agent submits the claim and tracks the status

opportunities.title: Clinical notes drafted from templates after visits
opportunities.description: An agent uses the dentist's short voice or text notes to draft a structured clinical note in the practice system. The dentist reviews, edits, and signs it, which reduces end-of-day typing.
before: Dentist records brief notes on paper or in the system
Dental nurse updates patient records during the appointment
Dentist writes fuller clinical notes after the visit
Staff checks notes for missing details
Dentist signs off the record
after: Dentist records short voice or text notes after the visit
Agent turns the notes into a structured draft
Agent checks the patient record for missing fields
Human: Dentist reviews, edits, and signs the note
Agent files the signed note in the practice system

opportunities.title: Treatment plan drafts prepared for dentist review
opportunities.description: An agent assembles the dentist's diagnosis, x-ray findings, and standard options into a treatment plan draft for the patient. The dentist reviews the clinical choices and approves the final plan.
before: Dentist reviews x-rays and writes treatment options
Dental nurse gathers patient history and notes
Staff types the treatment plan into a template
Dentist checks costs and options
Staff prints or emails the plan to the patient
after: Agent pulls diagnosis, x-ray notes, and patient history
Agent drafts options using approved templates
Human: Dentist reviews and confirms clinical choices
Agent updates costs, dates, and consent wording
Agent sends the plan to the patient for review

opportunities.title: No-show and late cancellation follow-up handled automatically
opportunities.description: An agent spots no-shows and late cancellations, sends a polite follow-up, and offers another appointment slot. It updates the no-show log and alerts the supervisor when a patient misses repeatedly.
before: Receptionist notices a missed appointment
Staff checks whether the patient called or emailed
Reception supervisor decides whether to charge or waive a fee
Receptionist calls or emails the patient
Staff updates the no-show log manually
after: Agent flags no-shows and late cancellations in the booking system
Agent sends a follow-up message with open slots
Patient picks a new time or explains the absence
Human: Reception supervisor reviews repeat no-shows and fee decisions
Agent updates the no-show log and daily report

opportunities.title: Supplier invoice coding and payment reminders run on a schedule
opportunities.description: An agent reads supplier invoices, matches them to purchase orders or clinic costs, and prepares them for approval. It also sends payment reminders and flags duplicate or missing invoices.
before: Finance assistant receives invoices by email or post
Staff enters invoice details into accounting software
Finance assistant matches invoices to orders or clinic costs
Finance manager approves payment runs
Staff chases missing invoices and credits
after: Agent reads invoice emails and extracts key details
Agent matches invoices to orders or clinic costs
Agent flags duplicates, missing details, or price changes
Human: Finance manager approves the payment run
Agent sends reminders and updates the supplier log

opportunities.title: Staff rota and training records kept up to date
opportunities.description: An agent drafts rotas across the three clinics from leave, clinic hours, and cover rules, then tracks training and compliance dates. The practice manager reviews and adjusts before publishing.
before: Practice manager collects leave requests and clinic needs
Staff builds the rota in a spreadsheet
Practice manager checks training and CQC dates manually
Staff emails the rota and updates changes
Practice manager tracks expiring certificates in a folder
after: Agent pulls leave requests, clinic hours, and cover rules
Agent drafts a rota with gaps and conflicts flagged
Human: Practice manager reviews and adjusts the rota
Agent publishes the rota and updates staff calendars
Agent tracks training dates and sends renewal reminders

opportunities.title: Patient data entry and document filing done with checks
opportunities.description: An agent reads forms, referrals, and insurance documents, then enters or files the standard details into the practice system. It flags anything unclear for an admin assistant to check.
before: Admin assistant receives forms, referrals, and insurance documents
Staff sorts documents by patient and clinic
Admin assistant types details into the practice system
Staff files paper or digital copies
Admin assistant checks for missing fields
after: Agent reads forms and extracts standard details
Agent enters details into the practice system or flags gaps
Agent files documents in the correct patient record
Human: Admin assistant checks flagged items and exceptions
Agent updates the filing log and daily count

roadmap.title: Prove booking, recall, and insurance agents at one clinic
items: Choose one clinic as the first test site
Set up the appointment booking agent with the phone system and booking system
Set up the recall reminder agent with the practice system and email
Set up the insurance claim agent with finance and insurer rules
Review daily outputs and fix errors before wider use

roadmap.title: Extend into clinical notes, no-shows, and patient filing
items: Add clinical note drafting for dentists and dental nurses
Add no-show and late cancellation follow-up at the front desk
Add patient data entry and document filing for admin assistants
Train staff on review steps and exception handling
Track time saved and error rates each week

roadmap.title: Connect finance, rota, and reporting across three clinics
items: Add supplier invoice coding and payment reminders for finance
Add rota and training record support for the practice manager
Connect agents to reporting for clinic performance
Roll out proven agents to all three clinics
Set a quarterly review of accuracy, privacy, and staff feedback

risks.risk: Patient data privacy and UK GDPR rules are not followed.
risks.mitigation: Use UK data storage, restrict access by role, complete a data protection review, and keep human approval for any patient-facing message or record change.

risks.risk: Clinical notes or treatment plan drafts contain errors.
risks.mitigation: Keep dentists responsible for all clinical decisions and require a dentist to review, edit, and sign every clinical note or plan.

risks.risk: Staff do not trust the agents or stop using them.
risks.mitigation: Start with one clinic, train the people who will review outputs, and share weekly examples of time saved and errors fixed.

risks.risk: The practice management software does not connect easily.
risks.mitigation: Begin with email, web forms, and CSV imports. Only add deeper integration after the agent has proven accurate for four to six weeks.

risks.risk: Exceptions are missed because staff rely too much on automation.
risks.mitigation: Run a daily exception report, keep named human owners for bookings, claims, and clinical notes, and review missed items in the weekly team meeting.
